claim: Node #115 routine 0x5d5a9d0 releases two shared-pointer collections in one holder, end to end: it drains a counted array (count at holder+0x00, element base at holder+0x88, stride 0x10, control pointer at element+0x08) from the last element down to count zero, then releases a begin/end vector (begin at holder+0x90, end at holder+0x98, stride 0x10, control pointer at element+0x08) in forward order and resets its end to its begin. Each control release decrements the count at control+0x08 (plain when the flag byte at 0x64ed290 is nonzero, atomic otherwise), calls the destroy helper 0x5d35070 when the old count is 1, and on the sentinel count 0x100000001 zeroes control+0x08 and calls the virtual slots 0x10 then 0x18. No buffer is freed and the holder itself is never freed.

callees.0x5d35070: shared destroy helper, called when a control's old count is 1

counted_array_phase.order: last element down to first; count ends at 0

release_shape.atomic_vs_plain: flag byte at 0x64ed290 nonzero selects the plain decrement, zero selects the atomic lock-xadd decrement
release_shape.destroy_helper: 0x5d35070, called when the old count is 1
release_shape.sentinel: count 0x100000001 zeroes control+0x08 and calls virtual slots 0x10 then 0x18 on the control's object

vector_phase.empty_vector: begin equal to end skips the loop and leaves end unchanged
vector_phase.end_reset: end set to begin after the loop

unknowns: Source-level types of the holder and the two collections; only sizes, strides and offsets are pinned.
The source meaning of the flag byte at 0x64ed290 beyond selecting the plain versus atomic decrement; only the selection is pinned.
Element+0x00 in both collections is never read by this routine; its role is not claimed.
What the caller function does before or after the call, and what the released objects represent; the neighbouring calls at 0x60d52f0 and 0x5d654c0 are not pinned here.
The destroy helper 0x5d35070 beyond its call contract (called with the control in rdi when the old count is 1); its internals are not re-pinned here.
